uncited: Relighting and Shading techniques address the problem of lighting inconsistency when compositing objects into neural radiance field (NeRF) scenes or synthesizing novel views under varying illumination conditions.

Unlike standard radiance field methods that treat radiance as a static view-dependent signal, this family explicitly models lighting interactions, inter-reflections, or shading correlations to enable physically plausible relighting and HDR synthesis.

It sets itself apart from direct relighting methods by either replacing object shading based on scene correlations [Shading Replacement for Relighting](6346-shading-replacement-for-relighting.md) or integrating surface rendering principles into the volume rendering framework to model irradiance [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).
The core mechanism involves decoupling or explicitly modeling the illumination component of the radiance field.
In standard NeRF, radiance $c(x, \mathbf{d})$ is a direct output of the network.
In this family, the representation is extended to account for how light interacts with geometry.
**Irradiance-Radiance Coupling**: Radiance is treated as both a signal conveying lighting information and a light source illuminating other pixels.
**Surface-Volume Integration**: Methods may integrate surface rendering principles (BRDF, normals) into the volumetric framework.
where $f_r$ is the BRDF, $\mathbf{n}$ is the surface normal, and $c_i(x, \omega_i)$ is the incoming radiance computed via volume rendering [Pano-NeRF](15013-pano-nerf.md).

**Shading Correlation**: In object insertion tasks, shading is inferred by correlating surface normals and shading values between the inserted object and the existing scene, avoiding explicit light source estimation [Shading Replacement for Relighting](6346-shading-replacement-for-relighting.md).
The concept of integrating lighting and shading into neural radiance fields has evolved to address limitations in standard NeRF regarding physical plausibility and dynamic lighting.
These methods build on the foundational NeRF architecture but modify the query and rendering process to include lighting-aware representations.
